newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks lower, Nasdaq market stagnant.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks lower, Nasdaq market stagnant.

text.p: Blue-chip stock were lower Thursday, relinquishing their modest early gains to profit-takers but lacking the conviction needed to make a decisive move either up or down.

At 1 p.m. EDT/1700 GMT, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 21.04 points at 7,336.19, retreating for a second straight day after racking up record high closes on Tuesday and last Friday. The market was closed Monday for Memorial Day.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines by a small margin on active trading of 270 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Nasdaq composite index was up 0.52 of a point at 1,410.70.
"Trading is a bit on the sloppy side," said Greg Nie, a senior vice president of technical research at Everen Securities.

A combination of negative earnings announcements and stock rating downgrades contributed to the market's uncertain sentiment, said John Gardner, chief equity strategist for Van Lieu Capital. "We are seeing a lot of fine-tuning going on," he said.
Dow component International Business Machines Corp. lost 1-3/8 to 88-1/2. Salomon Brothers said it downgraded the stock after this week's strong rally.
Nike Corp. was among shares hit by disappointing earnings warnings, falling 8-5/8 to 55.

The sportswear maker said its fourth-quarter results would fall below expectations, forecasting earnings of between 51 cents and 56 cents per share, compared with analysts' expectations of 69 cents a share. It cited a revenue shortfall.
Novell was off 5/16 at 7-3/4 after the computer software publisher posted an unexpected earnings loss in the latest quarter and said it planned to cut its work force.
"The market does not have a high degree of conviction," Gardner said. "It boils down to the fact that you now have to be very selective when buying individual names. It's a stock picker's market."

Joseph Battipaglio, chief investment officer at Gruntal & Co. also said the market had been strong in recent weeks and was due for a pull-back. "On a very short-term basis, it's profit-taking," he said.
"Stocks are holding in there but they have missed many opportunities on the upside as bonds have come back toward a 7 percent yield," Nie said.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury bond rose 9/32, lowering its yield to 7.01 percent from Wednesday's close of 7.03 percent.
Stocks could remain in limbo until they get some clues as to what the Federal Reserve's policy-makers will do at their next meeting in July, Gardner said.
For the stock market to rally again, it needs to display higher volume and decidely positive breadth, Nie said.
Among active issues, Boston Chicken Inc. lost 1-1/8 to 17. The company said it was not satisfied with sales momentum in its Boston Market stores.
Time Warner Inc. was down 1-1/2 at 47 on news that Canada's Seagram Co. Ltd. sold more than half of its stake in the company for $1.39 billion. Seagram rose 1/2 to 39-3/8 on the NYSE.
